title: 2024 CAQH Index Report — From Transactions to Trust

history.reason: Read in full (prior authorization and methodology sections) for the distribution investigation (issue #11)

source_type: industry administrative-transaction index (data from 600+ provider organizations and health plans covering 63% of insured lives; labor cost/time per transaction by channel)
reliability: The standard industry source for administrative transaction cost/time, contributed by both plans and providers and cited by federal agencies. CAQH's mission favors electronic transactions, so its savings framing is directional; per-transaction measurements are its core data product. Costs cover transaction labor only — not information gathering or follow-up.
findings: Provider time per prior authorization: 24 minutes when conducted manually (phone, fax, email) and 16 minutes via health plan portal — the highest portal time of any administrative transaction tracked.

Provider labor cost per manual prior authorization is $12.88 per transaction; the medical industry's remaining savings opportunity from full electronic adoption is $515 million, at an average of 14 minutes saved per transaction.

Channel mix is shifting: in 2024 manual prior-authorization volume fell 37%, portal volume rose 20%, and fully electronic volume rose 6%; providers most often request prior authorization via portal, and only about one-third of medical prior authorizations are fully electronic.
Specialists and behavioral health providers spend more time and money per prior authorization than generalists, due to case complexity.
Eligibility and benefit verification is nearly fully electronic for medical plans (96% adoption), in sharp contrast to prior authorization.
CMS rule CMS-0057 requires impacted payers to offer FHIR-based prior authorization APIs by January 1, 2027.
limitations: No practice-size segmentation: contributing organizations span all sizes and results are not broken out for small practices.
Per-transaction cost/time excludes gathering clinical information and follow-up work, so it understates the full per-request effort practices report in surveys.
National weighted estimates from participating organizations, not a random sample of practices.
